title: When Does It Actually Make Sense to Put AI Into Products?
abstract: Over the past few years, the tech industry has rushed to plug a new microchip into every device on the assumption that if you can add AI, you should. Smart vision toothbrushes , mood-reading household robots , and a host of physical products are invading consumers’ daily lives, reliant on artificial intelligence to learn, predict, and adjust our behavior. But as anyone who’s struggled to update the firmware in their fridge knows, AI doesn’t improve every product. Some product designers are asking where the line is between genuine innovation and a solution looking for a problem. Savannah Kunovsky leads a team of industrial product designers at Ideo , a design consultancy based in San Francisco focused on helping clients unpack when AI becomes a barrier rather than a breakthrough. Kunovsky spoke with IEEE Spectrum about the pressure to integrate AI in everything, where that integration goes wrong, and what companies can do to determine when an AI integration is—and isn’t—a smart choice. When AI makes products worse How much of the current wave of AI integration into physical products is driven by pressure from investors and shareholders to keep up with industry trends? Savannah Kunovsky : Some of it. Teams come to us feeling pressured to show they’re doing something with AI, sometimes because a CEO has promised the board an “AI story” before the next earnings call, or a competitor has just launched an AI-powered version of their product. In all cases, the first thing we do is step back and ask who the product is for and what they’re trying to do. Once that’s clear, the role AI should play, whether large, small, or invisible, usually becomes obvious. There is an appetite for this kind of grounding in the industry right now. People want to cut through the hype and see what works in practice. How do you distinguish between a genuinely helpful AI feature and a gimmick? Kunovsky : The test for an AI gimmick is the same test we’d apply to any product experience: Does it help someone do what they’re trying to do? Answering that means understanding how people would use the product in the real context they’ll be using it. Many companies look straight to large language models (LLMs) because that’s top of their mind, but there is a whole AI toolbox to draw from: computer vision, sensor fusion, on-device models, et cetera. Picking the right capability for the task matters as much as deciding whether to use AI in the first place. As a new interaction paradigm, AI is asking people to change their behavior, so it needs to be simple. When IDEO’s predecessor firm worked on Apple’s first mouse in the early 1980s , the team gave it only one button because people were learning a completely unfamiliar system and the interaction mechanism needed to be effortless. The wearable Humane AI pin used projection instead of a screen-based display, making a dramatic shift from the smartphone interface users already knew. Angel Garcia/Bloomberg/Getty Images In which products has AI made the user experience worse? Kunovsky : The clearest examples are products where AI replaced something that already worked. I have a lot of respect for Humane’s AI Pin as a provocation, but the technology [a screenless, wearable smartphone alternative that uses an AI assistant instead of apps] wasn’t ready . The Pin asked people to give up an interface they knew well for one that was slower and less reliable, which is a hard tradeoff to ask of anyone. You see versions of this problem everywhere—a voice assistant that mishears a simple command and turns off the wrong light, a customer service bot that keeps you in a loop when you just want a person. In cars, climate and volume controls moved onto touchscreens and voice menus, so something you used to do by feel now takes your eyes off the road. title: NSF’s X-Labs Program Draws Support From Charities and Investors
abstract: When the U.S. National Science Foundation began its X-Labs program in May, the agency said the higher-risk, higher-funded awards would create new kinds of partnerships that would confront urgent scientific and technological challenges. Now, the NSF is doubling down on the idea, with an announcement in October that charities, companies, and investment funds would provide X-Lab winners practical support such as laboratory space, software, shared equipment, and access to key data and expert guidance. The help provided by these organizations, which the NSF is calling “ consortium partners ,” will not give them ownership stakes in the X-Labs projects. The addition of the consortium partners may help the initial winners—who will be announced later in November or December and who receive US $1.5 million for a 9-month planning phase—reach the aggressive targets needed to compete for much larger $50 million multi-year grants. “It’s a way of telling X-Labs applicants you don’t need to reinvent the wheel, so you’re not spending half of your X-Labs money to go build or buy basic infrastructure,” says Matt Cimaglia , an investor in consortium partners Occam Foundry and Florida Quantum Center . NSF X-Labs Focus on AI, Computing, and More The NSF initially announced two focus areas for the X-Labs program: scientific instruments for sensing and imaging and photonic microchips for quantum systems . In September, the agency followed up with three additional areas in AI for physical devices , decoding biological sequences , and pushing the physical limits of computing . The NSF requires potential X-Labs award recipients to eventually demonstrate autonomy : Leaders for projects must be focused on the work full-time, for example, and must be able to make hiring and spending decisions independently from any university or commercial owners. That agility sets X-Labs apart, along with the risk appetite. Consortium partners saw the potential to provide infrastructure and operations support to allow X-Labs recipients to focus on research. “[We’re] very interested in the enabling structures of R&D,” says Joshua M. Greenberg , program director at the Sloan Foundation, one of the participating partners. Greenberg says that the foundation has supported multiple focused research organizations, or FROs, already. FROs are independent entities in the same vein as what the X-Labs program hopes to create. Unlike university laboratories or larger tech companies, FROs are founded with a time-limited purpose of advancing research in a well-defined area. Because they start with a clean slate, FROs may lack the infrastructure that university or corporate research groups might inherit. To address that lack of infrastructure, bioengineering service firm Ginkgo Bioworks , in Boston, is offering X-Lab winners up to $5 million worth of access to its “cloud lab,” says Jason Kelly , the firm’s CEO and founder. Ginkgo’s cloud lab can conduct complex and flexible laboratory work, and the company will also offer laboratory space and internal datasets that could be useful for training AI models. Kelly is enthusiastic about the potential for X-Labs, which he says have the potential to “pull platforms into existence” like the federal Human Genome Project once did, which enabled a lot of subsequent innovation. As scientific and technology companies become more powerful, Kelly says, it’s natural that governments should revisit how to involve them in government-led science. “The scale of companies is not like it was in the Vannevar Bush era [in the 1940s],” he says, “so how should the United States leverage those [much larger, more capable] companies? It’s silly to leave them on the sidelines.” In 1945, Vannevar Bush wrote an influential report that helped shape the modern NSF and U.S. federal science funding. title: AI Agents Are Testing the Limits of Zero-Trust Security
abstract: This article is brought to you by Queen’s University Belfast . Several teams around the globe are leveraging AI by creating a task force of agents managed by an orchestrator and creating applications to support risk assessment, client profiling, match making, and information yield with a slight overview of decision making. One of the important components for these agents is to ensure that the logs are managed and historic relevance is not being used to avoid skewing towards same decision making. Thus, the system is expected to keep checkpoints in place where agents are prompted to delete such historic relevance. However, despite such methodology in place, a future prompt could make the agents bring forward the information that was supposed to be deleted and can be tricked into revealing more information, which is a classic case of context recovery attack. So, the question raised here is: How can we trust that our instructions have been followed? And where is the proof? There is an element of utilizing zero-trust architectures (ZTA) for orchestrating and managing agentic activity, which simply means all agentic interactions use the core principle of “never trust,” “always verify.” ZTA components include a policy enforcement point (PEP) that has to be trusted to maintain trust across the system, so the question that remains is where is the component of zero-trust, and shall we trust the policies enforced by PEP? Having a pro-agentic approach and utilizing agents could be helpful with the right guardrails in place. Opening our systems to random agents that are being trained on off-the-shelf models and blindly relying on them can pose significant cyber risks. For example, vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces. Vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces. This opens critical discussions towards how vibe coding could interfere with the positioning and implementation of trusted execution of the agentic queries. Consider an autonomous web of agents that relies on agents’ inputs to drive the operations. When the system is operating under low tolerance of failure and with non-tracking based agentic workflows, it could be computationally expensive to trust and verify each query in real-time that leads to the common trade-offs of memory vs execution. Another risk to consider is the zero-day attack. When it happens, how will the system react? Would such an event be manageable without a total infrastructure breakdown? The scale of impact can be observed from over reliance on agentic ecosystems with only one trusted layer. This could mean that when failure occurs, the entire ecosystem could be exposed, just like there will be no autonomy if the backbone network is not available, which essentially means no layer to place trust. How quickly can de-authentication attacks occur? An in-house experiment done at Queen’s University Belfast (QUB) provided an initial understanding of how the scale of agentic attacks could mean a lower window of vulnerability. The team focused on very popular de-authentication attacks and with agentic orchestration, the swift rate to do de-authentication attacks could go as low as 2 to 3 seconds. This gives little to no time to react and decide on patching the system. There is another aspect of the large-scale agentic system, which establishes trust under asynchronous autonomy. Trust serves as a critical foundation for traceability. How would you ensure that all the agents operating towards a common goal are aligned and understand the delays associated with their goals? title: CEO Jensen Huang's job is suddenly on the line at Nvidia
abstract: Nvidia’s board is set to hold urgent talks about the future of its founder Jensen Huang after revelations that he had an affair with a top executive at the company, according to people familiar with the matter. The meeting on Wednesday comes amid a deepening scandal at the $4.2 trillion group, after Donald Trump said the FBI was investigating allegations that Huang was romantically involved with an alleged Chinese spy. The Nvidia chief executive had a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, the chipmaker’s vice-president of healthcare, according to two people familiar with the matter. Powell, a more than 18-year veteran at Nvidia, is among the company’s more prominent public figures. Read full article Comments

title: T-Mobile illegally imposed 50GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says
abstract: T-Mobile violated a New York state law by imposing a 50GB-per-month data cap and reducing speeds to less than a megabit per second on home Internet plans it is required to offer people with low incomes, New York government officials alleged. T-Mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days. The alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to T-Mobile's wireless home Internet service, not the company's mobile plans. Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement on Monday, saying that a state investigation found T-Mobile violated the New York Affordable Broadband Act (ABA). Read full article Comments

title: Anduril says its first satellite can see adversaries maneuver in orbital night
abstract: Anduril Industries has announced the successful demonstration of a new satellite-based sensor designed to track other spacecraft that may be hiding their maneuvers in Earth's shadow. Funded with Anduril's internal capital, the company's oven-sized satellite launched on a SpaceX rideshare mission in July with a package of tech demo payloads: an edge-compute processor, a power-management system adaptable to different mission types, and a long-wave infrared space sensor capable of detecting other objects in orbit. Anduril reported on the success of the tech demo mission Tuesday. The company's satellite, named Anduril-216, flies about 590 km (366 mi) above Earth, spending about one-third of each orbit in darkness. Anduril-216's night passes allow its infrared imager to shine. Read full article Comments

title: NASA's secret weapon in the lunar space race may be ... procurement reform?
abstract: Senior NASA officials held a lengthy news conference last weekend, laying out a series of lunar contract awards, new contract opportunities, and mission decisions. They followed one after the other: landers, nuclear-powered rovers, scouting drones, power generation, storage, and communication satellites. It never seemed to end. "Hopefully, we're keeping industry on their toes trying to catch up to all the solicitations we're doing," said Carlos García-Galán, manager of the Moon Base Program, more than 90 minutes into the news conference. "This is what it takes to do the Moon Base in the timeline we have set forth." Read full article Comments

title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
abstract: Top chip manufacturer TSMC is ready to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI. That would give the Taiwanese chipmaker direct stakes in leading AI developers, even as its own contract chipmaking business has profited enormously from the AI data center buildout. The chipmaker’s board approved plans to invest up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and another $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at the latter’s expected IPO price, according to Reuters . Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported. But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal. Read full article Comments

title: Trump admin loses fight to spy on random journalists’ LinkedIn DMs
abstract: The Trump administration’s fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can’t sweep in “a vast number of confidential sources” of random journalists “who have no conceivable relationship” to the Department of Justice’s investigation, an appeals court ruled Tuesday. The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted. The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. That left journalists unaware for far too long that their First Amendment rights had been compromised, judges ruled. Read full article Comments

title: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
abstract: The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players. That debate has exploded into a full-blown controversy in the indie game development space this week, as Big Walk developer House House has publicly and belatedly disclosed minimal AI use in its popular co-operative puzzle exploration game. This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. But the debate started to break into public view on Monday when 19 members of the 50-plus-member jury released a signed statement outlining a stance "declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity." Noting "a significant increase in the number of submitted games developer with generative AI tools," the group of jurors called out AI's ecological, economic, psychological, and labor harms in rejecting tools whose use, they said, is still "not a foregone conclusion in our industry." Read full article Comments

title: Apple is shuttering its 28-year-old online community forum
abstract: Apple’s online community forum will close on November 20. On Tuesday night, Apple posted a message to the Apple Support Community announcing the forum's closure: The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state. You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site . We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products. For 28 years, the forum has provided Apple users with a way to get quick technical advice about their products. That advice usually came from fellow users, though Apple employees occasionally chimed in. As with any community forum, the helpfulness and accuracy of the advice varied. Read full article Comments

title: IBM to offer access to a dual-processor quantum system in 2027
abstract: IBM's Quantum Developer's Conference is being held this week, and the company is using the gathering to provide an update to its roadmap: It is aiming to make error-corrected quantum computers before the decade is out. The changes greatly expand the scope of its next-generation Nighthawk general-use processors by adding a version with over 500 programmable qubits. At the same time, it's stepping back a bit on its plan to link multiple Nighthawk processors together, dropping the intended number of linked systems from nine to two. The total number of qubits planned for next year will remain the same; how the company is getting there, however, will be different. Read full article Comments

title: Trump wanted little Kei trucks for America, Toyota makes it happen
abstract: The idea that Americans should be offered a greater choice of smaller cars has support from strange bedfellows indeed. After all, who could forget President Trump—usually one to take a maximalist approach to any problem— announcing last year that he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars legal here in the US. Ars’ attempts to get DoT to tell us more about the potential influx of little vehicles have mostly fallen on deaf ears. But this week, there has been movement on the topic, with Toyota announcing that it will bring back the Scion brand with the KEI-01. What’s a Kei car? In the US, the preponderance of humongous SUVs is a consequence largely of government policies, specifically corporate average fuel economy standards that made it less profitable to sell smaller, efficient cars. Japan’s Kei cars are what happens if the government instead restricts the size, engine capacity, and power output. Read full article Comments

title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
abstract: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself. Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities. Read full article Comments

title: Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
abstract: Seagate doesn't think hybrid drives are done just yet. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the new FireCuda Forge line of storage drives. The new drives combine the high capacity of a traditional plattered HDD with the speed and responsiveness of a user-supplied solid-state drive (SSD). The new hybrid storage solution is Seagate's first to be powered and managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform. The FireCuda Forge is available right now through Seagate's web store , and comes in 8TB ($699) or 20TB ($899) HDD configurations—neither of which includes the required SSD. Users will have to bring their own SSD, with some specific restrictions. The FireCuda Forge is compatible with M.2 2280 NVMe drives that are PCIe Gen3 or higher. The maximum supported NVMe capacity is 1TB, which means that's as much data as you'll be able to dedicate to storage on the "fast side" of the hybrid setup. The NVMe will require minimum speeds of 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and a unit with DRAM cache is recommended. Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write speeds for the combined system, along with USB4 and support for Windows 11 and macOS 26+. Credit: Seagate Read full article Comments

title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
abstract: The US military is taking a new approach to prop up commercial launch companies as SpaceX looks to wind down its Falcon rocket program, suggesting defense officials see the workhorse rocket's retirement as a potential national security risk. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital has twice in the last two weeks announced it was sending cash to two of SpaceX's competitors in the launch business. First, on October 26, the office announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space. Military officials revealed a second $150 million Pentagon loan Tuesday for Rocket Lab. Stoke Space and Rocket Lab are the first two launch companies to receive significant support from the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), an organization established in 2022 to infuse companies developing "vital" national security technologies with capital. OSC has been on a loan spree in recent weeks, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to companies specializing in batteries, drones, and semiconductors. In the space sector, the office also provided a $150 million loan to LeoLabs , a commercial satellite tracking company, for production and deployment of radar units. Read full article Comments

title: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
abstract: Amazon is betting that many Ring customers will also want an AI-powered security drone and robot patrolling their homes or offices. But the company’s upcoming Ring Robotic products are also certain to intensify privacy concerns previously raised around a prior Amazon attempt to popularize a flying security camera. The Ring Rover Cam and Ring Drone Cam are expected to reach customers starting at the end of 2026 and in early 2027, respectively, according to an Amazon announcement posted on November 10. Amazon describes the devices as relying on an AI Pilot system that uses each device’s cameras along with “specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing” to plan patrol routes while autonomously navigating around obstacles such as furniture. Both devices also use that AI Pilot system to digitally map the floor plan of the customer’s home or business. This setup process occurs after the customer carries the Ring drone through their indoor spaces or allows the Ring Rover to do some autonomous exploration. Read full article Comments

title: Democrats oppose plan to stack FCC with Republicans, plan probes of Chairman Carr
abstract: Senate Democrats today opposed President Trump's nominee for an open Federal Communications Commission seat, and criticized Republicans for moving to confirm a new commissioner during the period before Democrats take control of Congress in January 2027. Democrats also plan to use their majority next year to launch probes of FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. "After the American people last week overwhelmingly rejected the MAGA agenda, there is no justification for this committee to advance partisan nominees during the lame-duck period," Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.) said today at the Commerce Committee's nomination hearing for Danielle Thumann Severs, Trump's pick to fill an empty commissioner's seat. Thumann Severs, an attorney and senior counsel to Carr, faced questions from Democrats about whether she supports Carr's attacks on TV broadcasters. Read full article Comments

title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
abstract: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it. You had one job Research from security firm Claroc shows that the exposed data includes things like internal business plans, ad proposals, medical exam results, galley checklists from a celebrity cruise line, and employee names and ID numbers. Ironically, some of the sensitive data comes from two-dozen apps built by SpaceXSI (the name of the now-merged SpaceX and xAI) itself. A small sampling of the documents revealed in the SpaceXSI apps—Claroc found 24 of them—include an onboarding plan, marked confidential, for a new member of SpaceXSI’s enterprise sales team, a sales territory map of 594 accounts, internal system addresses for sales team tools, and advertising proposals. Read full article Comments

title: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
abstract: Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called "big math" is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means , and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World , by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend. Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison. In 2005, Strogatz extended his study of synchronicity to the crowds that caused the wobbling of London's Millennium Bridge . An award-winning communicator, Strogatz wrote three series of columns on mathematics for The New York Times in 2010, 2012, and 2025 and hosted a podcast for Quanta magazine from 2020–2021. He has written four popular books: Sync (2003), The Calculus of Friendship (2009), The Joy of X (2012), and the New York Times bestseller Infinite Powers (2019). Read full article Comments

title: Google Fi adds support for a second 5G network, won't say which one
abstract: Google has announced a " super network " upgrade for its Fi cell service. For the past few years, Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network, but now it's adding support for a second 5G network. Oddly, Google refuses to say which one. Google's MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) launched in 2015 as Project Fi with support for both T-Mobile and Sprint service. The service initially only worked on Google's Nexus phones, which would switch between networks based on signal strength. After T-Mobile absorbed Sprint, Fi switched to being a single-network service in the US while continuing to hop between networks for international travel. With the super network, Google Fi is again a dual-carrier service stateside. Phones connected to Fi will be able to hop between T-Mobile 5G and a different 5G network to provide the best possible connectivity. Google's blog post announcing the change conspicuously doesn't mention either network, saying only that it supports "two of America’s best 5G cellular networks." Read full article Comments

title: Pixel phones getting new icon styles, Create My Widget, and more in November Pixel Drop
abstract: Google's Pixel phones get an update every month, but most are just security patches and bug fixes. The bigger changes are bundled into quarterly Pixel Drops, and one is rolling out today . The update brings a few new things, and many of the Gemini features previously exclusive to the latest Pixel phones will also expand to Google's Pixel 10 lineup. The Pixel 11 was Google's first foray into "Gemini Intelligence" branding, something we'll see a lot more of going forward. Some of the features under that heading were limited to Google's newest phones (and in some cases, Samsung's phones). The November Pixel Drop will expand these AI features to the Pixel 10 lineup, but importantly, that doesn't include the budget-oriented Pixel 10a . For starters, the Pixel 10 series will get the improved personalized suggestions (previously known as Magic Cue) that debuted on the Pixel 11 . This enables things like sending grocery lists to Google Keep from other apps and generating summaries from the context menu. Rambler, Google's AI-assisted voice input system, is also coming to the 2025 phones. Likewise, Gemini app automation will roll out on Pixel 10 with this update. This feature is still limited to select apps in rideshare, food delivery, travel, and a few other categories. Read full article Comments

abstract: 이 글에서 예로 든 스킬은 naver/design-to-ui 라는 이름의 오픈 소스로 공개되어 있습니다. 들어가며: 같은 모델, 다른 결과 AI 코딩 도구를 쓰다 보면 프롬프트에서 같은 설명을 매번 반복하게 됩니다. "이건 아이콘이니까 에셋으로 받아", "이건 그래프니까 Canvas로 그려", "색상은 하드코딩하지 말고 디자인 토큰을 써" 같은 설명이 그렇습니다. Figma 디자인을 Android 코드로 옮길 때도 마찬가지였습니다. 그래서 Claude의 스킬(Agent Skills) 기능이 공개되자마자 Figma 디자인을 Android UI로 변환하는 스킬을 만들기 시작했습니다. 목표는 프롬프트 한 번으로 완성도 높은 UI를 얻는 것이었습니다. 스킬의 효과는 생각보다 컸습니다. 2026년 3월, 같은 모델(Claude Opus 4.6)과 같은 프롬프트에 Figma Desktop MCP 서버까지 똑같이 쓰고 스킬만 바꿔 화면 하나를 조건마다 한 번씩 변환해 보았습니다. 그 결과는 다음과 같습니다. 조건 디자인 토큰(colorScheme) 참조 생성된 drawable 스킬 없음 8회 0개 범용 공식 스킬(Figma implement-design) 20회 0개 프로젝트 맞춤 스킬(figma-to-android) 39회 1개 colorScheme 참조가 많을수록 색상을 하드코딩하지 않고 디자인 토큰을 썼다는 뜻이고, drawable은 Figma의 아이콘을 실제 에셋 파일로 받아 왔는지를 보여 줍니다. 이 숫자를 어떻게 얻었는지는 계명 10 에서 다룹니다. Figma 공식 스킬이 부족해서 생긴 차이는 아닙니다. 범용 스킬은 프로젝트의 디자인 토큰과 에셋 규칙을 알 수 없고, 맞춤 스킬은 바로 그 공식 스킬 위에 프로젝트 규칙을 얹은 것입니다. 이 방식은 계명 2 에서 자세히 다룹니다. Figma 원본과 세 조건으로 변환한 날씨 화면(오토앱)을 나란히 놓으면 다음과 같습니다. 지역과 날씨 데이터는 Figma 시안의 예시 값이거나 캡처 시점의 실제 값이라 서로 다릅니다. Figma 원본 ① 스킬 없음 ② 범용 공식 스킬 ③ 프로젝트 맞춤 스킬 그림 1 Figma 원본(위)과 세 조건으로 변환한 날씨 화면(아래) 모델은 같았는데 결과물의 디테일은 확연히 달랐습니다. 예를 들어 '서울시 명동' 옆 위치 아이콘은 맞춤 스킬에서만 제대로 나왔고, 시간별 기온 그래프도 맞춤 스킬에서만 그려졌습니다. 다만 이 스킬을 틈틈이 만드는 데 3개월쯤 걸렸습니다. 이 글에서는 3개월 동안 알게 된 원칙 10가지를 정리했습니다. 처음부터 알았다면 그 시간을 크게 줄일 수 있었을 것입니다. 사내 Engineering Day에서 발표한 내용을 글로 옮기면서 발표에서 다 하지 못한 사례를 더했습니다. 스킬은 무엇이고 프롬프트와 무엇이 다른가 스킬은 특정 작업을 어떻게 해야 하는지 적어 둔 폴더입니다. 폴더에는 SKILL.md 파일이 하나 있고, 필요하면 참고 문서( references/ )와 스크립트( scripts/ )를 함께 넣습니다. Claude는 평소에는 스킬의 이름과 설명만 알고 있다가, 요청이 그 설명과 맞으면 SKILL.md 본문을 읽어 들여 그 지침에 따라 작업합니다. 프롬프트와의 차이는 세 가지입니다. 반복 설명이 사라집니다. 매번 프롬프트에 붙여 넣던 에셋 규칙과 변환 절차를 스킬에 한 번만 적어 두면 됩니다. 스크립트를 함께 넣을 수 있습니다. 말로 설명하기 어렵고 결과가 늘 같아야 하는 작업(예: SVG를 VectorDrawable로 변환)은 스크립트로 만들어 두고 Claude가 실행하게 합니다. 팀이 같이 키울 수 있습니다. 파일이라 버전 관리가 되고, 플러그인으로 묶어 배포할 수 있습니다. 이 글의 예시는 Claude Code 기준이지만, 같은 스킬 형식(Agent Skills)을 지원하는 다른 에이전트 도구에도 대부분 적용됩니다. 이 글에 자주 나오는 용어를 먼저 정리합니다. 용어 뜻 MCP(Model Context Protocol) AI 도구가 외부 프로그램(이 글에서는 Figma)과 데이터를 주고받는 표준 방식 frontmatter SKILL.md 맨 위에 스킬의 이름과 설명 등을 적는 메타데이터 영역 디자인 토큰 색상, 글자 크기처럼 디자인 시스템이 이름을 붙여 관리하는 값. Compose의 colorScheme.primary 처럼 colorScheme 에 모아 둔 색상 값이 그 예다. 토큰(LLM) AI 모델이 글을 처리하는 단위. 디자인 토큰과는 다르며, 스킬이 길수록 많이 쓴다. drawable, VectorDrawable Android 앱의 이미지 리소스와 그 벡터 형식 Canvas 코드로 직접 도형을 그리는 Android API gotcha Claude가 반복해서 실수하는 지점과 그 해결책을 적은 기록 에셋 A/B/C Figma의 그래픽 요소를 처리 방식에 따라 정적 에셋(A), 동적 비주얼(B), 기존 에셋(C)으로 나눈 것. 자세한 기준은 계명 6 에서 다룬다. 스킬 만들기 10계명 10계명은 사전 점검(1∼2), 본문 설계(3∼7), 검증과 개선(8∼10) 세 단계로 나뉩니다. 각 계명에는 스스로 던져 볼 핵심 질문과 figma-to-android 스킬을 만들며 겪은 실제 사례를 덧붙였습니다. 사전 점검 스킬을 만들기 전에 확인할 것들입니다. 스킬에 무엇을 담을지 직접 해 보며 찾고, 쓸 만한 스킬이 이미 있는지 살펴봅니다. 계명 1. 스킬부터 만들지 마라 — 먼저 직접 해 봐라 핵심 질문: 스킬 없이 해 보면서 무엇을 반복해서 설명했나? /skill-creator 에 원하는 스킬을 설명하면 형식에 맞는 스킬을 금방 만들어 줍니다. 하지만 그보다 먼저 스킬 없이 프롬프트만으로 작업을 해 봐야 합니다. 그러면서 세 가지를 관찰합니다. 매번 반복해서 설명하는 정보 Claude가 놓치는 것 사람이 손으로 고쳐 주는 패턴 이 세 가지가 스킬에 들어갈 내용입니다. Anthropic에서 Claude Code를 만드는 Thariq Shihipar도 Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills 에서 같은 이야기를 합니다. 뻔한 내용은 빼고 Claude의 기본 행동을 바꾸는 정보에 집중하라고 하면서, Anthropic의 좋은 스킬도 대부분 몇 줄짜리 지시와 gotcha 하나로 시작했다고 말합니다. 저는 반대로 했습니다. 처음부터 목표(Figma → Compose)와 필요할 것 같은 자료(Figma와 Compose의 매핑 정보)를 한꺼번에 주고 스킬을 만들어 달라고 했습니다. 그 결과 700줄이 넘는 스킬에서 출발했고, Claude는 긴 지시를 제대로 따르지 못했습니다. 이것이 3개월 동안 가장 큰 병목이었습니다. 그림 2 Compose와 XML을 함께 지원하도록 스킬을 다시 만들 때 쓴 프롬프트 다시 직접 날씨 화면을 변환해 보니 매번 "colorScheme을 써라", "SVG를 VectorDrawable로 변환해라", "기존 drawable이 있는지 확인해라"를 반복하고 있었습니다. 이 세 문장이 스킬의 핵심이 됐습니다. 단, 이미 절차를 잘 아는 워크플로를 스킬로 옮길 때는 "만들어 줘"로 시작해도 괜찮습니다. 계명 2. 기존 스킬 위에 쌓아라 — 바퀴를 재발명하지 마라 핵심 질문: 비슷한 공식 스킬이나 커뮤니티 스킬은 없나? 만들기 전에 비슷한 스킬이 이미 있는지부터 찾아봅니다. 검증된 구조 위에 도메인 특화 부분만 얹는 편이 훨씬 빠르고 안정적입니다. anthropics/skills : Anthropic 공식 스킬 저장소 figma/mcp-server-guide : Figma 공식 스킬과 MCP 가이드 사내 스킬 저장소 Figma가 공식 스킬 implement-design을 공개한 뒤에는 그 워크플로를 뼈대로 가져왔습니다. 이 스킬은 2026년 3월 figma-implement-design으로 이름이 바뀌었고 5월에 저장소에서 삭제됐지만, 워크플로를 figma-to-android 안에 옮겨 두었기 때문에 영향은 없었습니다. figma-to-android의 7단계는 Step 1(Node ID 추출), Step 2(디자인 컨텍스트), Step 3(스크린숏), Step 4(에셋 분

title: 우리 팀만의 스펙 주도 개발 정착기
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 스펙 주도 개발(SDD)을 팀 내 개발 정책으로 채택한 배경과 시행착오에 대해 소개합니다. ​ 발표 대상 스펙 주도 개발 도입을 고민중인 개발자 ​ 목차 배경 - SDD를 도입하게 된 이유 우리 팀이 채택한 SDD의 구조 팀 SDD 정책을 세우며 마주친 고민 일곱갈래 다음 고민과 남은 숙제 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: 로그인 화면, 이제 만들지 마세요 - n3r OIDC
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 n3r.iam을 OIDC Provider로 확장해 어떤 서비스에든 'n3r 계정으로 로그인'을 붙이는 방법을 소개하고, n3r의 프로젝트·역할 정보를 표준 토큰에 담아낸 설계 결정을 공유합니다. ​ <참고> 영상속 사내용어 n3r = 네이버 사내 쿠버네티스 기반 컨테이너 플랫폼 ​ ​ 발표 대상 n3r app에 사내 로그인과 권한 연동을 고려하는 개발자 표준 OIDC 위에 자체 권한 체계를 얹는 설계에 관심 있는 엔지니어 ​ 목차 Part 1. 로그인 화면을 만들 필요가 없는 이유 n3r OIDC가 필요한 사례 앱 하나를 띄울 때마다 반복되는 일 OIDC란 n3r에 이미 있는 계정과 권한 Part 2. n3r.iam OIDC 적용 방법 전체 로그인 flow 1단계: client 등록 2단계: 연동 설정 3단계: 토큰 안의 n3r 정보 n3r OIDC 연동 체크리스트 Part 3. 설계 결정과 다음 단계 표준을 그대로 따른 것 사용자의 project, role, group을 token에 포함 로그인하여 받은 Access Token으로 n3r API 호출 n3r API는 token의 role로 인가 role 변경은 access token 재발급하여 반영 다음 단계 및 정리 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: worklog-system 주간보고 자동화 구축 경험기

title: 크림에서 통합 임베딩(Universal Embedding)은 어떻게 쓰일까?
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 여러 엔티티를 한 공간에 담은 통합 임베딩과 범용 리트리벌이 크림 추천 곳곳에 쓰이는 방식, 운영하며 드러난 한계를 v2에서 해결한 과정, 그리고 확장 방향을 공유합니다. ​ 발표 대상 추천 시스템의 후보 생성(Retrieval) 단계에 관심 있으신 분들 여러 서비스·지면에서 함께 쓰는 공용 임베딩을 설계하고 운영하고 싶으신 ML 엔지니어 조건(필터)이 걸린 벡터 검색의 지연과 메모리를 줄이고 싶으신 분들 구좌·서비스마다 늘어나는 추천 모델을 줄이고 싶은 추천·검색 조직의 엔지니어와 기획자 ​ 키워드 Recommendation System / Candidate Generation (Retrieval) Universal Embedding (Bi-encoder · Contrastive Learning) Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) Filtered Vector Retrieval (Roaring Bitmap · Brute-force vs ANN) Embedding Serving Optimization ​ 목차 PART 1. 왜 통합 임베딩인가 2025년의 크림: 추천 구좌마다 모델이 따로 있었다 목표: 여러 목적에 쓸 수 있는 범용 임베딩 하나 구좌마다 ‘누구에게 · 무엇을 · 어떻게’가 다르다 통합 임베딩은 후보 생성에 직접, 랭킹에도 입력으로 설계 원칙: 모든 질문이 ‘벡터 + 조건’이 된다 PART 2. v1 모델 — 하나의 공간을 만들다 하나의 인코더가 검색어와 상품을 모두 읽는다 학습: InfoNCE를 받쳐 주는 일곱 가지 장치 학습은 상품 하나, 나머지는 모두 집계로 그림으로 보면: 모두가 상품 공간 위의 점 PART 3. v1 리트리벌 — 하나의 API로 꺼내 쓰다 질문 하나 = 요청 하나 조건별 상품 목록을 미리 만들어 두고 꺼내 쓰기 구좌 전용 모델 없이 붙은 첫 구좌들과 타겟 집단 추천 PART 4. 써 보니 드러난 v1의 한계 모델: 가끔 붕괴하고, 768차원은 무거웠다 리트리벌: 큰 조건을 감당하지 못했다 리트리벌: 조건을 자유롭게 조합할 수 없었다 v1의 한계, 한눈에 PART 5. v2 — 한계를 하나씩 걷어내다 모델 1차: 학습을 안정시키다 모델 2차: 하나의 벡터, 여러 해상도 (MRL) 좌표계: 회전으로 맞추려 했지만, 통하지 않았다 필터: Roaring Bitmap으로 조건을 실행할 때 조합 왜 근사 검색(ANN)이 아니라 후보 전부를 계산하나 점수 계산: 계산량은 그대로, 메모리 낭비만 없앴다 결과: 응답 지연은 약 4배 빠르게, 메모리는 1/6로 API: 조건 칸 하나 → 조건 리스트 v1의 한계 → v2의 처방 PART 6. 지금의 쓰임과 다음 확장 지금: 하나의 API가 채우는 지면과 구좌 비슷한 브랜드: 브랜드 벡터만으로는 부족했다 리트리벌 밖에서도 같은 벡터 다음으로 — 멀티벡터, 지면 확장, 마케팅 타겟팅 ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: 딸깍으로 안되는 Multi-interest 개발기

title: 컨테이너처럼 쓰고, VM처럼 격리하기

title: 실행은 격리하고, 세션은 이어간다: 망분리 환경의 Agent Platform 설계기
abstract: 초기 Agent Platform의 대화 화면. 사용자가 Agent를 선택하고 업무를 요청합니다. “지난달과 같은 기준으로 이번 달 데이터도 비교해줘.” 데이터를 분석하다 보면 자주 받는 요청입니다. 지난번에 쓴 쿼리를 찾아 기간을 바꾸고, 실행 결과를 비교해야 하죠. 빠진 데이터는 없는지, 집계 기준은 그대로인지도 확인해야 합니다. AI Platform 팀은 사람이 매번 반복하던 이 과정을 에이전트가 처리하도록 만들고 싶었습니다. 토스는 「 전자금융감독규정 」의 망분리 요건에 따라 금융 업무를 처리하는 내부망과 인터넷 업무 환경을 분리해 운영하고 있습니다. 자동화하려던 분석에 필요한 데이터도 내부망에 있었고, 외부로 옮길 수 없었습니다. 사람이 내부 도구로 하던 조회와 가공을 대신하려면, 에이전트가 내부망에서 코드를 실행하고 데이터를 분석할 수 있어야 했습니다. 그렇다고 에이전트에게 내부망의 모든 파일과 시스템을 열어줄 수는 없었습니다. 모델이 만든 코드가 작업과 관계없는 데이터를 읽거나 파일을 잘못 수정할 수도 있기 때문입니다. 프롬프트로 주의를 주는 것만으로는 이런 실수를 막기 어려웠습니다. 그래서 에이전트의 코드를 샌드박스 안에서 실행하고, 작업에 필요한 파일과 시스템에만 접근하도록 제한했습니다. 이전에 하던 작업을 이어가는 것도 중요했습니다. “지난달과 같은 기준으로 비교해줘”라는 요청을 처리하려면, 지난번에 사용한 코드와 집계 기준을 알아야 하니까요. 매번 새 환경에서 시작한다면 사용자는 코드를 다시 준비하고 분석 기준도 다시 설명해야 합니다. 사용자가 같은 내용을 매번 준비하지 않아도 되도록, 작업 파일과 대화 상태를 보관하기로 했습니다. 이 글에서는 이 두 가지 요구를 바탕으로 Agent Platform을 설계한 과정을 소개합니다. 샌드박스에서 파일과 네트워크 접근을 어떻게 제한했는지 실행 환경이 바뀌어도 작업을 계속할 수 있도록 파일과 대화 상태를 어떻게 관리했는지 모델이 만든 코드는 어디에서 실행할까 플랫폼 관리 기능은 Workspace 밖에 두고, 모델이 만든 코드와 명령은 Workspace 안의 제한된 환경에서 실행합니다. *구조도에 나오는 GenAI Gateway와 MCP Gateway의 역할이 궁금하다면 이전 글 을 참고해 주세요. 모델은 어떤 코드를 실행할지 결정할 수 있지만, 스스로 프로세스를 띄우거나 파일을 고치지는 않습니다. 모델의 응답에 따라 도구를 실행하고, 그 결과를 다시 모델에 전달하는 프로그램이 필요하죠. 이 과정을 반복하는 프로그램을 하네스(harness) 라고 부릅니다. 분석 코드에 오류가 나면 그 내용을 모델에 전달하고, 수정한 코드를 다시 실행하는 것도 하네스가 맡습니다. 모델과 도구를 반복해서 호출하는 일은 기존 하네스에 맡겼습니다. 플랫폼은 요청자가 누구인지 확인하고, 작업에 필요한 실행 환경과 접근 권한을 준비합니다. 이렇게 역할을 나누면 하네스를 교체하더라도 사용자 관리나 저장소 연결을 다시 구현할 필요가 없습니다. 한 사용자가 여러 에이전트와 대화할 수 있으므로, 실행할 때는 누구의 작업 공간인지, 어떤 에이전트의 대화인지 구분해야 합니다. Workspace : 사용자마다 제공하는 개인 작업 공간 Agent : 업무 지침과 사용할 도구를 설정한 에이전트 Session : 각 Agent와 나누는 개별 대화 예를 들어 한 Workspace 안에 데이터 분석 Agent와 문서 작성 Agent를 두고, 분석 Agent와 월별로 다른 대화를 나눌 수 있습니다. Agent나 대화마다 실행 환경을 만들면 환경 준비와 저장소 연결도 반복해야 합니다. 이 반복을 줄이기 위해 사용자마다 Kubernetes의 실행 단위인 Pod를 만들고, Workspace의 실행 환경으로 재사용하기로 했습니다. 하나의 Pod를 함께 쓰더라도 Agent마다 접근할 수 있는 파일과 시스템은 제한해야 합니다. Agent의 지침과 도구 설정에 따라 실제 작업을 수행하는 것은 하네스입니다. 그래서 하네스를 격리하고, 그 안에서 실행한 도구와 코드에도 같은 접근 제한이 적용되도록 했습니다. Workspace의 실행 환경은 오픈소스 OpenSandbox 로 관리합니다. OpenSandbox가 Kubernetes에 Workspace별 Pod를 만들고 종료하는 일을 맡습니다. Runtime은 Pod 안에서 하네스를 바로 실행하지 않습니다. 먼저 bubblewrap으로 접근할 폴더와 통신 경로를 제한한 환경을 만들고, 그 안에서 하네스와 도구를 실행합니다. 사용자가 화면에서 분석을 요청하면 다음 순서로 실행을 준비합니다. Server 가 사용자와 리소스 접근 권한을 확인 Runner 가 해당 Workspace의 실행 환경을 준비하고 Runtime에 실행 설정을 전달 Runtime 이 설정에 맞춰 하네스를 격리하고 실행 실행 준비가 끝나면 하네스가 모델과 도구를 호출하며 작업을 진행합니다. 사용자는 화면에서 응답과 실행 결과를 확인할 수 있습니다. Server와 Runner는 Workspace Pod 밖에서 동작합니다. 하네스에는 업무에 필요한 입력과 도구를 제공하지만, 플랫폼 DB의 인증정보는 넘기지 않습니다. 분석 코드를 실행하는 데 다른 사용자의 설정이나 플랫폼 관리 기능에 접근할 권한까지 필요한 것은 아니니까요. 같은 Pod 안에서 Agent의 접근 범위를 나누기 Runtime은 Agent마다 허용한 폴더를 연결하고, 격리된 환경의 통신을 HTTP 프록시로 연결합니다. 같은 Workspace를 사용해도 각 Agent가 접근할 수 있는 파일은 다릅니다. 분석 Agent는 분석에 필요한 참고 문서를 읽을 수 있어야 합니다. 그렇다고 문서 작성 Agent의 작업 파일까지 마음대로 바꿀 수 있어서는 안 되겠죠. 화면에서 도구 목록을 숨기거나 파일 읽기 도구에서만 권한을 확인하는 것으로는 부족했습니다. 하네스가 셸 명령이나 직접 작성한 프로그램으로 같은 파일을 열 수도 있기 때문입니다. 그래서 도구의 종류와 관계없이, 코드를 실행하는 프로세스 자체의 접근 범위를 제한 하기로 했습니다. Runtime은 bubblewrap 을 사용해 하네스마다 별도의 Linux namespace를 구성합니다. namespace는 프로세스마다 파일시스템의 마운트 구성, 프로세스 목록, 네트워크 등을 격리할 수 있는 Linux 기능입니다. Agent마다 별도 VM을 두면 게스트 커널까지 나눌 수 있습니다. 다만 VM별로 이미지와 작업 볼륨을 준비하고, 생성과 종료를 플랫폼의 실행 흐름에 연결해야 합니다. 저희가 필요로 한 것은 Workspace의 실행 환경을 재사용하면서, 그 안에서 하네스마다 파일과 통신 접근 범위를 다르게 설정하는 것이었습니다. 이를 위해 기존 Kubernetes와 OpenSandbox 구성 안에서 bubblewrap으로 하네스를 격리하는 방식을 선택했습니다. 실행 환경의 생성과 종료는 Workspace 단위로 관리하고, 하네스를 실행할 때 허용한 폴더와 통신 경로만 연결했습니다. Agent마다 별도의 게스트 운영체제를 준비하고 관리하지 않아도 필요한 접근 제한을 적용할 수 있었습니다. 다만 호스트 커널을 공유하므로 VM과 같은 커널 격리를 제공하지는 않습니다. 두 방식의 차이는 다음과 같습니다. 방식 장점 플랫폼에서 준비하고 관리할 것 Agent마다 별도 VM 사용 Agent마다 게스트 커널을 따로 사용하는 격리 환경을 구성할 수 있음 VM 생성과 종료, 이미지 준비, 작업 볼륨 연결을 플랫폼 실행 흐름과 연동 Workspace Pod 안에서 namespace 사용 기존 Workspace 안에서 하네스마다 파일과 네트워크 접근 범위를 설정할 수 있음 기존 Kubernetes/OpenSandbox 구성을 활용하면서, 하네스별 파일/네트워크/실행 권한을 설정하고 격리 동작을 검증 같은 Pod 안에서 실행하더라도, 각 하네스에 필요한 파일과 통신 경로만 제공해야 합니다. 이를 위해 Runtime은 하네스를 실행할 때 다음 세 가지를 제한합니다. 1️⃣ 접근할 수 있는 파일 실행에 필요한 기본 파일 외에는 Agent의 작업 폴더, 사용자가 추가로 허용한 폴더, 현재 세션의 상태가 저장된 경로만 마운트합니다. 마운트는 실제 디렉터리를

title: TASTE, 토스의 추천 파운데이션 플랫폼
abstract: 금융 상품에 관심이 있는 사람을 찾는 모델, 푸시를 클릭할 사람을 찾는 모델, 좋아할 미니앱을 추천하는 모델. 풀어야 할 문제는 다르지만, 이해해야 하는 대상은 모두 같은 토스의 사용자입니다. 토스에 쌓이는 방대하고 서로 다른 데이터를 충분히 학습하여 배운 내용을 여러 추천 문제에 활용할 수는 없을까요? TASTE(Toss Automated Standard Targeting Engine) 는 이 질문에서 시작했습니다. 사용자의 다양한 행동을 함께 예측하고, 그 과정에서 배운 ‘사용자 표현’을 다른 서비스 모델에 전달하고자 했습니다. 여러 서비스의 온오프라인 실험에서 이 표현이 예측에 도움이 된다는 것까지 확인했습니다. 이 글에서는 여러 행동을 함께 학습하고, 그 과정에서 얻은 사용자 표현을 다른 추천 모델에 전달하며, 이를 다시 개선하는 과정 을 소개합니다. 한 번 배운 사용자 정보를 여러 추천 문제에 활용하는 것, 이것이 저희가 생각하는 추천 파운데이션 모델의 출발점입니다. 같은 사용자를 모델마다 다시 배우고 있었습니다 토스에는 금융중개, 광고, 쇼핑, 결제, Apps in Toss 등 여러 서비스가 있습니다. 서비스가 늘어날수록 클릭, 구매, 전환 등을 예측하는 모델도 늘어납니다. 모델마다 목표는 달라도 사용하는 사용자 정보는 겹치는 부분이 많습니다. 나이와 같은 속성, 앱에서 이용한 기능, 소비 이력 등이 대표적입니다. 각 모델은 이 정보를 자신의 예측에 필요한 형태로 가공하고 학습합니다. 같은 정보를 모델마다 따로 준비하고 학습하면서 중복 작업이 생겼습니다. 데이터를 충분히 활용하는 일도 쉽지 않았습니다. 토스는 월간 활성 사용자(MAU)가 2천만 명을 넘어, 주요 서버 로그만 해도 하루에 수십억 건 이상 쌓입니다. 사용자 한 명을 이해하기 위해 살펴봐야 할 정보도 방대합니다. 데이터의 성격도 제각각입니다. 마이데이터는 수십 개의 API를 통해 들어오며, 데이터마다 수집 시점과 정보를 확보할 수 있는 사용자 범위가 다릅니다. 외부 앱 이용 정보를 담은 MMP 데이터는 이벤트가 지나치게 많거나, 반대로 너무 적기도 합니다. 서버 로그와 마이데이터, MMP 데이터는 활용하고 분석할 수 있는 동의 조건도 모두 다릅니다. 결국 각 모델은 예측 문제를 풀기에 앞서, 이 방대하고 서로 다른 데이터를 어떻게 모으고 학습할지부터 해결해야 했습니다. 서비스별 예측 모델은 응답 시간 등 서비스가 요구하는 수준(SLA)을 맞춰야 해서 상대적으로 크기가 작습니다. 이런 제약 아래에서 개별 모델이 방대한 정보를 충분히 학습하기는 쉽지 않습니다. 그래서 서비스 중인 모델들이 예측에 도움이 되는 사용자 정보를 놓치고 있을 수 있다는 가설을 세웠습니다. 모델을 합치는 것만으로는 성능이 좋아지지 않았습니다 “ 여러 모델에 필요한 사용자 표현을 한 번에 학습하고, 그 결과를 여러 목적에 활용할 수 있을까? ” 먼저 주요 앱이벤트를 동시에 예측하는 멀티태스크 학습을 시도했습니다. 사용자 정보를 예측에 필요한 표현으로 바꾸는 인코더(Encoder)를 공유하고, 그 뒤에 결제나 특정 서비스 이용 등 과제별 예측을 담당하는 헤드(Head)를 붙이는 방식입니다. 같은 정보를 받아도 과제마다 필요한 부분은 다릅니다. 과제별로 필요한 정보를 다르게 조합할 수 있도록, 처음에는 MMoE(Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts) 구조를 시도했습니다. 빠르게 가능성을 살펴보기 위해 초기에는 학습 사용자를 100만 명으로 줄였습니다. 사용자 수를 줄인 영향을 살펴볼 수 있도록, 기존 모델에 사용하던 LightGBM도 100만 명 규모로 학습했습니다. 같은 사용자 수로 학습한 두 모델을 비교했을 때, MMoE의 성능(AUROC)은 과제별로 따로 학습한 LightGBM보다 낮았습니다. 이 결과만으로는 여러 과제를 함께 학습하는 방식의 이점을 확인하기 어려웠습니다. 학습 데이터와 모델을 확장하자 성능이 올랐습니다 하지만 저희는 다른 가설을 세웠습니다. “ 한 모델이 여러 행동을 동시에 예측하려면, 각 행동을 따로 학습할 때보다 더 많은 데이터가 필요한 것 아닐까? ” 공동학습 자체의 한계로 결론짓기 전에, 더 많은 사용자와 더 풍부한 행동 정보를 학습해보기로 했습니다. 우선 학습 대상을 100만 명에서 학습에 사용할 수 있는 전체 사용자로 넓혔습니다. 사용자 요약 정보도 기존 1,000여 개에서 2,000개 이상으로 늘렸습니다. 요약 정보에 담기지 않은 행동의 흐름도 배울 수 있도록, 최근 앱이벤트 시퀀스를 Causal Transformer로 읽고 압축했습니다. 늘어난 입력에 맞춰 모델 구조도 개선했습니다. 요약 정보를 처리하는 인코더에는 DCN-V2를, 과제별 예측을 담당하는 부분에는 PLE(Progressive Layered Extraction)를 사용했습니다. 학습 사용자 규모와 입력 피처, 모델 구조를 확대한 뒤에는 기존 모델의 성능을 넘어설 수 있었습니다. 공통 앱이벤트 예측에서 Macro Recall@5k의 상대 개선율은 약 35.1%입니다. 초기의 낮은 성능을 공동학습의 한계로 받아들이지 않고 가설을 세워 실험한 결과입니다. 사용자 요약 정보를 2,000개 이상 사용하면서 새로운 의문도 생겼습니다. 요약 정보가 충분하다면 시퀀스 모듈은 없어도 되지 않을까요? 이를 확인하기 위해 시퀀스 모듈을 제거한 별도 실험을 진행했고, Macro Recall@5k가 상대적으로 7.6% 낮아지는 것을 확인했습니다. 많은 요약 정보를 사용하더라도, 시퀀스를 직접 학습하면 예측에 도움이 된다는 정보를 추가로 얻었습니다. 소비까지 함께 배우며 목적에 맞는 구조를 찾았습니다 앱이벤트 공동학습의 성과를 바탕으로, 주요 소비 이벤트까지 학습 범위를 넓혔습니다. 앱이벤트 시퀀스가 요약 정보를 보완했던 것처럼, 소비도 이력을 직접 학습하면 도움이 될 것이라고 생각했습니다. 그래서 미래 소비를 예측하는 과제와 함께, 브랜드·카테고리 등의 소비 시퀀스를 읽는 인코더를 추가했습니다. 하지만 한 모델에서 모두 학습하자 과제별 성과가 달라졌습니다. 소비 예측은 기존 개별 모델보다 좋아졌지만, 앱이벤트의 Macro Recall@5k는 앱이벤트만 한 번에 학습했을 때보다 낮아졌습니다. 앱이벤트와 소비는 행동의 성격도, 정답 데이터가 들어오는 시점도 크게 달랐습니다. 두 목적을 예측하는 데 필요한 표현과 학습 방식도 다를 수 있었습니다. 그래서 각 목적에 맞는 표현을 따로 학습하면 성능을 개선할 수 있을 것 이라는 가설을 세웠습니다. 입력 정보는 함께 활용하되, 앱이벤트와 소비를 예측하는 모델은 인코더부터 따로 학습했습니다. 두 모델 모두 앱이벤트 이력, 소비 이력, 사용자 요약 정보를 받으며, 각 모델 안에서는 여전히 여러 앱이벤트 또는 소비 과제를 함께 학습합니다. 모델별로 구조를 탐색하고 최적화해, 각 목적에 맞는 학습 방식을 찾았습니다. 목적을 나누고 각 모델의 구조와 학습 방법을 개선한 결과, 앱이벤트의 Macro Recall@5k는 단일 모델 TASTE보다 8.7% 높아졌습니다. 소비 예측은 같은 지표에서 기존 모델 대비 브랜드 33.9%, 중분류 111%, 소분류 65.8% 개선됐습니다. 여러 과제를 함께 학습하는 이점을 살리면서도, 목적에 맞게 모델을 나누고 최적화해 각 서비스에 필요한 성능을 확보할 수 있었습니다. 학습한 모델을 실제 운영에 연결했습니다 TASTE가 제공하는 결과물은 크게 두 가지입니다. 하나는 모델이 직접 계산한 행동별 예측 확률이고, 다른 하나는 학습한 사용자 정보를 담은 임베딩입니다. 먼저 예측 확률을 실제 운영에 활용한 사례를 소개하겠습니다. 우선 여러 과제를 함께 학습하면서 개별 모델마다 반복하던 데이터 준비·학습·추론 작업을 통합하고, 중복되는 인프라 사용과 운영 부담을 줄였습니다. 이렇게 생성한 확률값은 목표 행동을 할 가능성이 높은 사용자를 찾는 데 활용했습니다. 토스에서 IM(Intelligence Manager)은 홈 상단 배너를 노출하고 푸시, SMS·LMS, 브랜드톡을 발송하는 통합 메시지 발송 허브입니다. 캠페인 담당자가 많은 시간을 쓰는 일 중 하나는 ‘누구에게 보낼까’를 정하는 것이었습니다. 같은 푸시라도 목표에 따라 어떤 행동 이

title: Anthropic launches roadshow for proposed initial public offering
abstract: Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.

title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. Together, these results support explicit competing explanations as a way for discovery agents to resolve more scientific questions from the same evidence and validation budget.

title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
abstract: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls. These agents achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, exceeding observed expert performance. LLM-guided feature discovery generally outperforms direct reasoning, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves open-weight models, enabling them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models in our evaluations. These results establish Pyrite as a challenging test of pose-ranking ability and highlight LLM-guided feature discovery as a promising approach to interpret and combine the outputs of computational chemistry tools.

title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
abstract: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
abstract: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.

title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
abstract: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations. Furthermore, our generative formulation enables inference-time search over multiple plausible scene hypotheses, using geometric evidence extracted from observed RGB frames to improve geometric prediction without ground truth geometry. We demonstrate UGG's effectiveness over non-unified baselines across camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction, including in challenging sparse observation settings. Code and visualizations are available at https://ugg-model.github.io/

title: DnNP: Denoising Input Uncertainty in Neural Processes
abstract: Neural Processes (NPs) are flexible meta-learning models capable of uncertainty quantification across diverse applications. However, the standard NP framework assumes access to noise-free inputs. This is unrealistic in many practical settings, where sensor noise or measurement errors are unavoidable. This discrepancy between model assumptions and real-world data can significantly degrade prediction quality and uncertainty estimates. We introduce Denoising Neural Processes (DnNPs), a principled extension of the NP framework that explicitly models input uncertainty. We train DnNPs via variational inference. DnNPs jointly learn to denoise corrupted inputs and perform meta-learning, making them robust to noisy training data. We demonstrate DnNPs' effectiveness on both synthetic and real-world datasets, showing consistent improvements in prediction and uncertainty quantification compared to standard NPs. On PM2.5 spatial interpolation from real-world air quality sensors, DnNP reduces RMSE by up to 30% and NLL by up to 73% relative to standard NPs. We also provide theoretical grounding: we show that the Bayes-optimal predictor under noisy inputs belongs to the DnNP model class, and that plug-in models with fixed observation variance incur an irreducible KL divergence gap that DnNP provably avoids.

title: Causal Concept Explanations for Deep Neural Models
abstract: Concept-based explanations in neural models are important for the development, certification, and adoption of autonomous systems. Yet, interpretability remains correlational. Without methods to guide and quantify causal relationships between explanations, a concept explanation can be provided without being necessary or sufficient for the observed output thereby appearing correct while misleading. We introduce Causal Concept Wrapper Network (CCW-Net), the first use of interventional mediation analysis from fields such as economics, medicine, and epidemiology as a training objective to align causal effects of concept-based explanations with a model's output. We further apply mediation analysis as an evaluation tool to quantify, per concept label combination, how much of any model's output is causally attributable to each concept explanation. As a training objective, CCW-Net shapes a model's concept representations such that they are both necessary and sufficient for the outputs they are credited with and independent of other concepts' contributions. Counterfactual concept representations anchor a set of causal alignment criteria: necessity, sufficiency, and independence. Necessity drives irrelevant concept effects toward zero, sufficiency ensures relevant concept representations fully reconstruct a model's output, and independence enforces the total effect decomposes linearly across concepts. We evaluate CCW-Net across aircraft control, driving, and image classification. CCW-Net provides a step toward concept-based explanations that are not merely interpretable, but quantifiably causal, supporting safer evaluation, certification, and deployment of transparent and trustworthy neural models.

title: The Unused Input: The Initial State as a Conditioning Interface for Recurrent TSFMs
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast unseen series without task-specific training. Increasingly they are built on recurrent backbones, whose constant per-step cost makes long-context inference cheap, and which, unlike transformers, carry a state. A recurrent backbone computes its prediction from two inputs: the observed context window and the initial recurrent state. In practice only the first is utilised and the initial state is unused by convention. We ask whether the initial state can be utilised in recurrent TSFMs. Using the xLSTM-based zero-shot forecaster TiRex as a case study, we freeze the backbone and train only a small head that writes a context vector into the initial state, so that any change in accuracy is attributable to the injected state rather than to adapted weights. A spectral summary of the input window, learned once and applied unchanged to every series, lowers mean GiftEval MASE by 0.175%, with every seed improving, which neither a parameter-matched LoRA adapter nor a learnable static state reproduces. An embedding of text attached to each series, evaluated on six MoTime datasets, reveals two roles for the state. As a per-dataset adaptation surface, a static state lowers MASE by 0.04-6.96% of the zero-shot baseline (8-70% of the gain of full fine-tuning). As a channel for exogenous information, the text-conditioned state lowers it by a further 0.15-0.41% of the zero-shot baseline on four of six datasets and, combined with a LoRA adapter, exceeds full fine-tuning, which has no access to the text, on one of them. In TiRex, the effect concentrates in the mLSTM blocks and is strongest at short context. The results are preliminary and the improvements small, but they point to the initial state as a direction for further research.

title: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning with Pooling-Induced Substructures
abstract: Hierarchical graph-level tasks that require reasoning over substructures that extend beyond local neighborhoods are posing challenges for standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). While graph pooling aims to address this by coarsening graphs into hierarchical representations, existing methods often fail to explicitly preserve the substructures they induce, leading to inconsistent empirical performance. Moreover, evaluating such approaches remains challenging due to the lack of benchmarks with explicit hierarchical structure. We propose Pooled-Substructure-Aware GNNs, an approach to graph pooling that explicitly preserves and processes substructures uncovered by structure-based pooling schemes. We show that this design enhances the expressive power of pooling-based GNNs in the sense of the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) test. To enable principled evaluation, we introduce two new synthetic datasets with controllable hierarchical structure and propose a metric to characterize the prevalence of hierarchical patterns in real-world graph-level benchmarks. On tasks with relevant hierarchical structure, our approach outperforms matched pooling baselines, while remaining competitive on structurally simpler benchmarks. Code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/lsbicego/PSA-GNN/.

title: Personalized Memory Rubrics: Learning What to Remember per User via Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment
abstract: Long-horizon personalized agents maintain an evolving memory by continuously deciding what to add, modify, or discard. However, learning an optimal update policy remains challenging. Conventional training relies solely on terminal question-answering accuracy, yielding a coarse feedback signal that treats all intermediate updates identically. Furthermore, update utility is inherently user-specific, as identical memory actions may yield opposite effects across different user personas. Existing methods fail to address this heterogeneity, relying on globally shared evaluation standards with at most a single scalar intermediate reward. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{Personalized Memory Rubrics} (\textbf{PMR}), a framework that translates terminal feedback into fine-grained, per-step, and per-user credit assignment. PMR decomposes evaluation into a universal layer capturing cross-persona failure patterns and a per-user adaptive layer modeling individual traits as a specialized delta over the universal baseline. Through \textbf{Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment}, PMR redistributes credit at the token level, selectively amplifying validated decisions on successful trajectories while falling back to standard policy optimization on failed ones to avoid unreliable attribution. The rubric and memory policy \textbf{co-evolve} in a closed loop with anti-circularity guarantees. Crucially, PMR incurs zero inference overhead, operating without any rubric or external judge during deployment. Extensive experiments across four benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains over strong memory-augmented baselines.

title: LUMIR: Decoupled Multimodal Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Data for Next-POI Recommendation
abstract: As multimodal tourism-related information collected from heterogeneous data sources has become increasingly available, learning effective representations has attracted attention for improving recommendation performance. Existing approaches often tightly couple multimodal fusion with the architecture and optimization objective of a specific downstream model, which limits the generality and reusability of the learned representations. To address these limitations, we propose LUMIR, a decoupled multimodal representation learning framework based on contrastive learning. Multimodal information collected from heterogeneous data sources is first semantically unified into a shared textual representation space using large language models (LLMs). An interaction-aware fusion mechanism is then designed to model cross-modal interactions, while sequential signals are incorporated as a structural constraint to guide representation learning. To evaluate the learned representations, experiments are conducted on a multimodal point-of-interest (POI) dataset under the next-POI recommendation setting across multiple sequential recommendation backbones. The results show that LUMIR consistently outperforms existing multimodal fusion baselines in both accuracy-oriented and beyond-accuracy metrics, demonstrating that decoupling representation learning from downstream optimization provides an effective paradigm for learning reusable multimodal representations. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/wzehui/LUMIR.

title: Data Quality Challenges in Multimodal Tourism Recommender Systems
abstract: Modern recommender systems increasingly consider diverse data modalities to enhance model performance. However, the quality of the underlying multimodal data (e.g. data from social media platforms) has received limited attention so far. Focusing on tourism recommendation, we examine real-world challenges encountered when using datasets from Yelp and Instagram. Issues include noise from fake reviews, hallucinated content from LLMs, modality contradictions, and demographic bias. We outline future directions such as quality-aware fusion, structured and controlled LLM-based content generation to reduce hallucinations, and user group differentiation to improve the robustness and reliability of multimodal recommendation systems.

title: Beyond Proxy Metrics: MLLMs as Human Surrogates for Explainable AI Evaluation
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has expanded into a broad and impactful research area, but the fundamental question of how best to evaluate explanation techniques has proven frustratingly elusive. Methodologies typically revolve around either proxy metrics which tell us little about the utility of an explanation, or human evaluation which---while generally considered the gold standard---is expensive, difficult to scale, and challenging to reproduce. In this paper, we investigate if Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can act as surrogate human participants to automate the evaluation of XAI. To do this, we first propose a ``purpose-grounded'' evaluation framework with metrics applicable to both MLLMs and human users alike. Then, we offer some conceptual insights as to why and when we can trust these models to automate this process. Lastly, we conduct extensive empirical testing across five purpose-grounded areas such as model improvement and fourteen popular MLLMs. Results indicate that all models trend positively, but OpenAI and Qwen models generally show higher alignment compared to other variants, which would be the recommended choices in practice. We expect our insights not to replace user testing, but rather to help XAI researchers complement their current evaluation methodologies and move the field away from heavy reliance on proxy metrics for measuring explanation utility.

title: Dual-Space Preconditioning for Variational Inequalities and Root-Finding Problems
abstract: This paper develops a dual-space preconditioning framework for variational inequalities and root-finding problems beyond classical cocoercivity and Lipschitz continuity assumptions. To this end, we introduce both a novel cocoercivity-type condition and a relaxed Lipschitz continuity condition, and derive convergence of deterministic and stochastic methods under these generalized conditions. For isotropic preconditioners, the resulting algorithms can be interpreted as variable-stepsize variants of classical methods, extending recent analyses based on $(L_0, L_1)$-type growth conditions while allowing simpler proofs and larger stepsize ranges. We also show that the framework naturally handles variational inequalities through weak Minty-type arguments. Finally, we study the associated continuous-time dynamics and derive a variational and optimal control interpretation of the preconditioned flow. Overall, the results show that dual-space preconditioning provides a flexible mechanism for designing and analyzing operator methods beyond the standard Euclidean Lipschitz setting.

title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
abstract: Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns. We optimize these mediators for correctness, informativeness, and linguistic quality through preference optimization, and evaluate the resulting explanations with human-calibrated metrics derived from separate human-labeled datasets. On the MovieLens-1M dataset, across multiple counterfactual generators and language models, the resulting summaries achieve high overall linguistic quality, while the strongest semantic results are obtained with high-success CFX methods such as ACCENT and SPINRec. Direct Preference Optimization improves the semantic metrics in almost all evaluated settings.

title: Where to Approximate in Neurosymbolic Inference?
abstract: Probabilistic neurosymbolic methods rely on weighted model counting (WMC) to combine neural predictors with symbolic constraints. Exact WMC is #P-hard and typically scales poorly, so many methods resort to approximations. By unifying existing approaches under a three-step bottom-up approximate compilation pipeline, we study where approximation budget is best allocated. Inspired by tensor networks, we instantiate two steps with tensor train decompositions and derive new pipelines that exactly multiply approximated factors and recompress their products via SVD- or interpolation-based schemes. Across six tasks in Sudoku, arithmetic reasoning, and scene understanding, and across increasing problem sizes, our pipelines produce WMC estimates orders-of-magnitude more accurate than prior methods. This translates into stronger downstream learning on tasks where reasoning relies on tight interactions between symbolic factors, where cruder approximations ignore these dependencies. Our pipelines open novel design space for effective approximate compilation of challenging probabilistic reasoning tasks.

title: Plug-and-Play ADMM for Inverse Problems with Flow Matching Denoiser
abstract: Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods with generative priors have achieved strong performance in inverse problems, with recent flow matching models enabling fast and scalable reconstruction. However, a key challenge in PnP methods is maintaining consistency between data fidelity updates and the learned generative prior, as data-consistency steps can move iterates away from the flow trajectory. We propose an ADMM-based PnP framework for flow matching priors that enforces stronger consistency between the measurement model and the prior through auxiliary variables and dual updates. In addition, we introduce a trajectory correction mechanism that restores consistency with the flow via a combination of deterministic and stochastic projections. Our method provides a more principled integration of flow priors within PnP frameworks, achieving high-quality reconstructions with reduced computational cost.

title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
abstract: Manifold embedding for data visualisation is dominated by a small set of hand-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms. Their design targets are fixed at development time, resulting in inflexible algorithmic behaviour that cannot be readily steered towards user-specified structural priorities. Hand-designing new embedding algorithms to address user priority requires highly specialised expertise and is time consuming. To address autonomous algorithm design tailored to user preference, we introduce an agentic algorithm generation pipeline AutoManifold. It composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimisation primitives, supported by multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) orchestration. AutoManifold conditions every stage of its design on user-specified structural preservation preferences, and iteratively refines the algorithm configuration through an LLM-guided, metric-grounded iterative loop. We compare the generated algorithms against the three strongest and most frequently used SOTA methods (t-SNE, UMAP, and PaCMAP) on real-world datasets spanning different difficulty regimes under identical evaluation infrastructure. The results demonstrate that LLM-driven, priority-conditioned algorithm synthesis can move beyond hyperparameter tuning, producing genuinely new algorithms that outperform traditional hand-designed methods in their ability to steer towards user-specified properties without compromising the intrinsic structure in the original data. The code of AutoManifold is available at https://github.com/buraksusam/AutoManifold_NeurIPS2026.

title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference
abstract: Privacy concerns have been raised in Large Language Models (LLM) inference when models are deployed in Cloud Service Providers (CSP). Homomorphic encryption (HE) offers a promising solution by enabling secure inference directly over encrypted inputs. However, the high computational overhead of HE remains a major bottleneck. To address this challenge, we propose MOAI, an efficient HE-based, non-interactive framework for secure transformer inference. MOAI gains significant efficiency improvement from: (1) a novel evaluation flow that combines column and diagonal packing with consistent strategies across all layers, eliminating expensive format conversions. (2) rotation-free algorithms for Softmax and LayerNorm that significantly reduce the number of costly HE rotations, removing 2,448 HE rotations in BERT-base inference. (3) Column packing removes rotations in plaintext-ciphertext matrix multiplications and interleaved batching further reduces the rotations in ciphertext-ciphertext matrix multiplications. MOAI uses at least 1.7x fewer HE rotations compared to the state-of-the-art works across all matrix multiplications of BERT-base. As a result, we achieve a $52.8 \%$ reduction in evaluation time compared to the state-of-the-art HE-based non-interactive secure transformer inference, THOR (Moon et al., CCS 25). We then apply MOAI on the Powerformer's framework and achieve a $55.7 \%$ reduction in evaluation time compared to Powerformer (Park et al., ACL 25), which approximates Softmax and LayerNorm with simpler functions in transformer and proposes HE-based non-interactive transformer inference. We report an amortized time of 2.36 minutes per input on a single GPU environment. We show the extendibility by applying MOAI in LLaMA-3-8B. Our implementation is publicly available as open source.

title: Curriculum proof repair with learned counterexamples
abstract: Language models (LMs) have substantially lowered the barrier to applying formal verification for building reliable and secure software. Existing approaches commonly follow the verifier-in-the-loop paradigm, but the verifier often provides only coarse, binary pass/fail feedback, which offers little actionable signal on how the proof should be repaired. Recent work shows that counterexamples provide more actionable feedback by grounding proof failures in concrete program states, but generating useful ones at inference time requires costly iterative refinement. We present TopoVerus, an LM-based framework for Verus proof repair that internalizes counterexample-guided diagnosis as a model capability, producing useful counterexamples in a single pass. Our key insight is to train counterexample generation not as a standalone validation task, but as a data-driven diagnostic objective: a counterexample is useful when conditioning on it helps the model produce a safe, verifier-passing proof.
